projects.institutes: Namibia Institute of Public Health; Ministry of Health and Social Services; WHO CC GOARN; IANPHI
projects.title: TwiNit 3.0 – Namibia–RKI twinning

projects.institutes: CHU Bouaké; Université Alassane Ouattara; Helmholtz Institute for One Health
projects.title: PAcCI – Public Health Actions for Côte d'Ivoire
projects.summary: Capacity building in infectious disease surveillance and prevention: digital tools, infection control, laboratory diagnostics, One Health and outbreak management.
projects.note: Project page lists an end date of 31 Dec 2025.

projects.institutes: Laboratoire d'Analyses Médicales Malagasy (LA2M); Ministry of Health
projects.title: STRAIN – diagnostics of highly infectious bacteria
projects.summary: Strengthening laboratory diagnostics for Yersinia pestis (plague) and Vibrio cholerae in Madagascar.

projects.institutes: INSP Guinea; National Public Health Agency Sierra Leone; Africa CDC; CEA-PCMT; COMAHS
projects.title: PREPARE – effectiveness of public health and social measures
projects.summary: Multi-country pilot in Africa to develop protocols that measure how well public health and social measures work during health emergencies.

projects.institutes: Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC)
projects.title: NiCaDe III – capacity development with NCDC
projects.summary: Third phase of building the Nigeria CDC's capacity for sustainable infectious disease preparedness and response.

projects.title: COPE II – community-based One Health strategy
projects.summary: Phase II (assessment phase) of a community-based, participatory One Health strategy in Nigeria.

projects.title: STEP – immunisation policy capacity
projects.summary: Building technical capacity for evidence-based decisions on immunisation policies in 16 countries of the WHO European Region.

projects.institutes: Ghana Health Service; University of Ghana; WHO Country Office
projects.title: Global Health Preparedness Programme in Ghana
projects.summary: IHR assessment (Joint External Evaluation 2016), simulation exercises, national action plan for health security, event-based surveillance, chemical-event preparedness and an environmental-health module for field epidemiology training.
projects.note: Page describes the collaboration as continuing; no end date given.

projects.institutes: WHO; IANPHI; Africa CDC; ECDC; US CDC
projects.title: NIPH global health security partner countries
projects.summary: NIPH lists Malawi, Moldova and Palestine (besides Ghana) as partner countries for IHR capacity, national public health institute strengthening and emergency preparedness.
projects.note: Dates per country not stated on the page.

projects.institutes: Ethiopian Public Health Institute (EPHI)
projects.title: Peer-to-peer exchange NIPH – EPHI
projects.summary: An NIPH delegation met staff and leadership of the Ethiopian Public Health Institute in a peer-to-peer collaboration.
projects.note: EPHI reported in Aug 2024 that the collaboration runs under NIPH's BIS programme since 2021; BIS phase 1 ended June 2025 and a second phase depended on donor approval.

projects.institutes: National public health institutes and ministries of health; Africa CDC (regional)
projects.title: IHR Strengthening Project
projects.summary: DHSC-funded programme, implemented by UKHSA, to help partner countries prevent, detect and respond to health threats and meet IHR (2005) requirements. Also works regionally via Africa CDC, in the Eastern Mediterranean and in South-East Asia.
projects.note: Classified as 'implementation' on DevTracker; start/end dates not shown.

projects.institutes: Ethiopian Public Health Institute; NCDC Nigeria; INS Mozambique; Zambia NPHI; others
projects.title: CDC support to national public health institute development
projects.summary: CDC's overview of countries where it helps establish or strengthen national public health institutes (strategic planning, surveillance, laboratory systems, workforce, emergency response).
projects.note: Undated overview page; individual country engagements may have ended.

projects.institutes: IANPHI; WHO/Europe (Ukraine)
projects.title: CDC–IANPHI partnership for NPHIs
projects.summary: Since 2011: planning support for Zambia's NPHI (2015), consultation for Burkina Faso's institute (2018), an assessment of Ukraine's Public Health Center (2019) and Staged Development Tool workshops in several countries.
projects.note: Source is a 2021 anniversary article.

projects.institutes: IANPHI; US CDC
projects.title: African NPHI peer learning around Mozambique's INS
projects.summary: Delegations from Malawi and Zambia (2016) and Sierra Leone and Uganda (2017) visited Mozambique's national institute to learn from its set-up.

projects.institutes: Kenya Ministry of Health (DPPHS); IANPHI
projects.title: Kenya–Canada peer-to-peer partnership
projects.summary: PHAC hosted a study tour for Kenya's new Directorate of Preventive and Promotive Health Services on how a national public health agency is set up.

projects.institutes: French Government (signed by France's ambassador to Ethiopia)
projects.title: Africa CDC – France MoU
projects.summary: MoU of 14 Sep 2023 covering support for Africa CDC and new national public health institutes, surveillance, local production of vaccines and diagnostics, workforce training and research partnerships.
projects.note: Partner is the French state, not a public health institute.

projects.institutes: European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC, Stockholm)
projects.title: Africa CDC – ECDC MoU
projects.summary: MoU (reported March 2026) on surveillance, risk assessment, emergency preparedness, AMR, vaccine-preventable diseases, modelling, laboratories and training. A new five-year Team Europe initiative was reported to start in May 2026 after the previous partnership ended in April 2026.

projects.institutes: Africa CDC
projects.title: China CDC – Africa CDC cooperation
projects.summary: Reciprocal visits in Nov and Dec 2024 on disease prevention and control, surveillance and the mpox response.
projects.note: No formal agreement mentioned in the source.

projects.institutes: Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR)
projects.title: RIVM – ICMR letter of intent
projects.summary: Five-year letter of intent (following an MoU of June 2025) on climate change and health, infectious diseases including AMR, vector-borne diseases, One Health and surveillance, with joint projects and capacity building.
projects.note: Signature dates on the document are ambiguous (2026).

projects.institutes: African Union Scientific, Technical and Research Commission
projects.title: ICMR – African Union MoU
projects.summary: MoU of 2019 on South–South health research collaboration, capacity building and development of drugs, diagnostics and vaccines for regional priority diseases.
projects.note: Partner is the African Union (seat Addis Ababa), not an NPHI.

projects.actor: Univ. of Copenhagen / DTU / Univ. of Gothenburg
projects.institutes: National Institute for Medical Research (NIMR); SUZA; UDSM; KCRI; NMCP; ZAMEP
projects.title: Pre-VBD – climate-based early warning for malaria and dengue
projects.summary: Early warning system forecasting malaria, dengue and chikungunya risk as climate changes, being integrated into Tanzania's DHIS2. Universities rather than an NPHI lead from the European side; included as the closest climate-and-health match found for Tanzania. The Robert Koch Institute is not named.
projects.note: Press release of 27 Nov 2025.

projects.institutes: RIVM (National Institute for Public Health and the Environment)
projects.title: China CDC – RIVM memorandum of understanding
projects.summary: Agreement signed during an RIVM delegation visit to Beijing covering ten areas, among them infectious and chronic disease control, health promotion and cross-border outbreak response; the visit included a One Health seminar.
projects.note: Signed 25 May 2026; no term stated.

projects.institutes: Robert Koch Institute
projects.title: China CDC – Robert Koch Institute memorandum of understanding
projects.summary: Five-year cooperation agreement between the two national institutes on infectious diseases, health emergencies, non-communicable diseases, laboratory safety and workforce training.
projects.note: Signed by video link on 23 July 2024 for five years; end year derived from that term.

projects.institutes: Instituto de Medicina Tropical Pedro Kourí (IPK)
projects.title: China CDC – IPK Cuba memorandum of understanding
projects.summary: Agreement between China CDC and Cuba's tropical medicine institute, both IANPHI members, on tropical disease control, laboratory diagnostics, emergency response and training.
projects.note: Exact signing date not stated; page updated 26 Aug 2026.

projects.institutes: Instituto Nacional de Salud (INS) Colombia
projects.title: China CDC – INS Colombia technical exchange
projects.summary: First bilateral video meeting between the two institutes, framed as the start of cooperation on surveillance, emergency preparedness and laboratory capacity. No formal agreement is mentioned.
projects.note: Meeting held 25 Nov 2025.

projects.institutes: Africa CDC; national public health institutes of the four countries
projects.title: SPhIRhA – Strengthening Public Health Institutes for Resilience in Health in Africa
projects.summary: Sida-funded four-year project, coordinated by the Swedish agency together with Africa CDC, to strengthen four African NPHIs with a particular focus on sexual and reproductive health and rights.
projects.note: Announced April 2025 as a four-year project; exact start and end not given.

projects.institutes: Nine national public health institutes (incl. NPHIL Liberia)
projects.title: Africa CDC NPHI centres of excellence
projects.summary: Africa CDC funded nine national public health institutes to act as regional hubs offering technical assistance, training and mentoring to peers, with plans to twin them with European NPHIs through ECDC.
projects.note: US$1.6 million announced Feb 2025.

projects.institutes: CAS-TWAS Centre of Excellence for Emerging Infectious Diseases (CEEID)
projects.title: Fiocruz – CEEID Sino-Brazilian infectious disease centre
projects.summary: Scientific cooperation agreement to set up a joint research and prevention centre for infectious diseases with sites in Beijing and Rio de Janeiro, covering arboviruses, influenza, TB, vaccines and diagnostics.
projects.note: Signed in Beijing, April 2023; no term stated.

projects.actor: Finnish Institute for Health and Welfare (THL)
projects.institutes: Public Health Wales (UK partner); THL (coordinator); RIVM; NIJZ; AGES; Switzerland took part as a collaborating partner with its own funding
projects.title: SHARP JA – Strengthened International Health Regulations and Preparedness
projects.summary: A joint action to help countries implement the International Health Regulations and strengthen preparedness for serious cross-border health threats, including laboratory capacity and chemical threats.
projects.note: 26 partner countries, including 21 EU members and Norway. Belgium, Bulgaria, Iceland and Switzerland were collaborating partners with their own funding. Coordinator and dates (04.2019–09.2023) are from AGES: https://www.ages.at/en/research/project-highlights/sharp

projects.institutes: Sciensano; RIVM; NIJZ; Serbian and UK partner institutes not named on the source page
projects.title: JA TERROR – Preparedness and response to biological and chemical terror attacks
projects.summary: Strengthened cross-sector preparedness of health systems for biological and chemical terror attacks, including links between health and security services and a simulation exercise.
projects.note: 17 countries took part, including 14 EU members and Norway. Dates (05.2021–04.2024) are from Sciensano's project page.

projects.actor: Italy-led consortium (lead author from Istituto Superiore di Sanità; the formal coordinating body is not confirmed)
projects.institutes: Norwegian Institute of Public Health (FHI); ISS; Serbian and Bosnian partner institutes not named
projects.title: JAHEE – Joint Action Health Equity Europe
projects.summary: Helped participating countries design and pilot policies to reduce health inequalities in areas such as monitoring, healthy living environments, migration and health systems.
projects.note: 24 countries. The UK took part while it was still an EU member, before Brexit. Norway (EEA) also took part.

projects.actor: National Institute of Public Health of Slovenia (NIJZ)
projects.institutes: Institute of Public Health of Serbia 'Dr Milan Jovanović Batut'; NIJZ (coordinator); Sciensano
projects.title: iPAAC – Innovative Partnership for Action Against Cancer
projects.summary: Supported countries in implementing innovative cancer control approaches, such as cancer plans, genomics, screening and care pathways.
projects.note: 44 partner institutions from 24 countries. Extended to 31 Dec 2021 because of COVID-19.

projects.actor: Norwegian Institute of Public Health (FHI) and Norwegian Directorate of Health
projects.institutes: Ukrainian partner institute not named on the source page; FHI; Sciensano; ISS
projects.title: JA PreventNCD – Cancer and other NCD prevention: action on health determinants
projects.summary: A large joint action that tackles shared risk factors for cancer and other non-communicable diseases through policy, health-determinant and individual-level interventions.
projects.note: More than 100 partners from 25 countries: 22 EU Member States plus Iceland, Norway and Ukraine.

projects.institutes: Ukrainian partner institute not named; ISS (coordinator); Sciensano; Santé publique France; NIJZ
projects.title: JACARDI – Joint Action on Cardiovascular Diseases and Diabetes
projects.summary: Pilots and scales up interventions to prevent and manage cardiovascular disease and diabetes, from health literacy to screening and patient pathways.
projects.note: 21 European countries take part, including Ukraine. Runs 1 Nov 2023 to 31 Oct 2027.

projects.institutes: Ukrainian and Moldovan partner institutes not named on the source pages; RIVM coordinates the Dutch participation
projects.title: EUCanScreen – European Joint Action on Cancer Screening
projects.summary: Supports countries in implementing the updated EU cancer screening recommendations, covering breast, cervical, colorectal, lung, prostate and gastric cancer.
projects.note: 29 countries: 25 EU members plus Ukraine, Moldova, Norway and Iceland. Sources disagree on dates: RIVM gives 04.2024–03.2027, Rīga Stradiņš University gives 05.2024–04.2028. The coordinator is from https://science.rsu.lv/en/projects/joint-action-on-the-new-eu-cancer-screening-scheme-implementation/

projects.actor: Inserm (with the French Ministry of Health)
projects.institutes: Ukrainian partner institute not named; NPHIs among the more than 120 partners
projects.title: EU-JAMRAI 2 – Joint Action on Antimicrobial Resistance and Healthcare-Associated Infections
projects.summary: A One Health joint action to turn EU and national AMR action plans into practice, covering stewardship, infection prevention, surveillance and awareness.
projects.note: More than 120 partners from 30 countries: EU Member States plus Iceland, Norway and Ukraine. Runs 48 months from 1 Jan 2024. The coordinator is a research institute, not an NPHI.

projects.institutes: Robert Koch Institute; University of Sydney; London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine; IANPHI; Lancet Countdown; WHO; MCC
projects.title: Tracking Extreme Heat Impacts (GHHIN activity)
projects.summary: A Global Heat Health Information Network workstream led by staff from Santé publique France and RKI. It is harmonising heat-health indicators and heat-impact registries, and it will produce guidance for NPHIs on setting up heat-health surveillance, plus peer-to-peer pairing between early adopters and countries still building capacity.
projects.note: Countries are inferred from the activity leads' affiliations; the page itself names no countries. The page lists UK partner LSHTM but not UKHSA.

projects.institutes: Africa CDC (Addis Ababa; continental scope)
projects.title: NIPH support to Africa CDC's Climate Change and Health Strategic Framework (BIS programme)
projects.summary: Under the Norad-funded BIS programme, NIPH is helping Africa CDC put its 2025 climate and health strategic framework into practice. The work includes baseline assessments of member states' capacities and communities of practice between countries.
projects.note: The NIPH–Africa CDC MoU dates from 2022. Africa CDC launched the framework in July 2025, and BIS phase 2 runs until 2029. Ethiopia is listed only because Africa CDC is headquartered there. This is separate from the excluded NIPH–EPHI item, but both fall under the same BIS programme.

projects.actor: IANPHI (Climate Change and Public Health Thematic Committee)
projects.institutes: World Meteorological Organization (Geneva); committee chaired by Santé publique France
projects.title: IANPHI–WMO MoU and heat-health indicator declaration
projects.summary: IANPHI's climate committee helped sign an MoU with WMO in December 2025, after a joint workshop in London in July 2025. An AFD-funded workshop in Lyon in November 2025 produced a draft NPHI declaration on heat-health indicators, due for member endorsement in 2026.
projects.note: IANPHI is an association of NPHIs, not an NPHI; its secretariat has been hosted by RKI since 2025. The committee has about 30 member countries.

projects.institutes: China CDC; other BRICS member and partner NPHIs (not named); IANPHI
projects.title: First Conference of BRICS National Public Health Institutes
projects.summary: As holder of Brazil's 2025 BRICS chairship, Fiocruz convened the BRICS NPHIs: a virtual meeting in April 2025, then an in-person conference in Rio in September 2025. Climate change and health was one of five themes, and China CDC chaired a session on climate, health and equity ahead of COP30.
projects.note: Only China's attendance is confirmed by name; more than 20 countries attended in total. No formal agreement was reported.

projects.institutes: Africa CDC (Addis Ababa; continental scope)
projects.title: Africa CDC–Fiocruz Memorandum of Understanding
projects.summary: An MoU signed on the margins of WHA78 in Geneva (May 2025) to strengthen African NPHIs, One Health surveillance, translational research, local manufacturing and public health law, implemented through a joint action plan.
projects.note: The article gives the date as 20 May without a year; WHA78 and Fiocruz's 125th anniversary place it in 2025. The MoU carries no financial commitments. Ethiopia is listed only as Africa CDC's HQ country. This is separate from the excluded Fiocruz–CEEID item.

projects.institutes: Caribbean Public Health Agency (CARPHA); CARPHA reference laboratories in Trinidad and Tobago, Jamaica and Saint Lucia; PAHO (parallel project)
projects.title: Caribbean Antimicrobial Resistance Alliance (CARA)
projects.summary: A Fleming Fund-supported partnership between UKHSA and CARPHA that expands AMR reference laboratory services and builds a region-wide digital AMR surveillance platform. It was formally launched in Barbados in May 2025.
projects.note: A UKHSA board paper (AB-25-039) says CARA launched in November 2024 with funding for up to two more years. Saint Lucia (not in the atlas) and Barbados (launch venue) are mentioned only here.

projects.institutes: Institute of Public Health Albania; National Institute of Public Health Kosovo; Institute of Public Health of Montenegro; Institute of Public Health North Macedonia
projects.title: SPHERE – Strengthening public health systems in the Western Balkans (GHPP)
projects.summary: An RKI-implemented GHPP project with four Western Balkan NPHIs on pandemic preparedness, IHR, laboratory diagnostics, surveillance and AMR monitoring. It builds on cooperation that began in 2016.

projects.institutes: WHO HQ AMR Department; WHO EURO AMR Division (partner-country institutes not named)
projects.title: AMR-EFFECT – RKI support strategy for implementing global AMR commitments (GHPP)
projects.summary: A GHPP project to help partner countries analyse AMR and healthcare-associated infection surveillance data and use them for policy, with a focus on digital tools and One Health approaches.

projects.institutes: Ministry of Health and Social Services Namibia; Jordan Center for Disease Control (JCDC); Fiocruz
projects.title: SCAPHeR – Applied public health research capacity in GHPP regions (GHPP)
projects.summary: Builds applied public health research capacity among public-sector staff and communities of practice in the WHO AFRO and EMRO regions, with Fiocruz contributing. It follows on from the earlier GHPP project CARe.
projects.note: Budget about EUR 1.17 million.

projects.institutes: Medical Research Institute; University of Colombo; Colombo North Teaching Hospital; Ministry of Health; WHO Country Office Sri Lanka
projects.title: IDEA-ALL – Alliance for identifying emerging pathogens (GHPP)
projects.summary: Strengthens laboratory diagnostics, surveillance and infection prevention in Sri Lanka, with a focus on zoonotic viral infections. It succeeds the IDEAnet project.

projects.institutes: National Veterinary Research Institute Vom; Federal University of Agriculture Abeokuta; Central Veterinary Laboratory Windhoek; University of Namibia; Zanzibar Agriculture and Livestock Research Institute; KCCR Kumasi; WHO AFRO; Robert Koch Institute; BNITM
projects.title: OH NET – One Health networks against AMR and zoonoses (GHPP)
projects.summary: An FLI-led GHPP project, with RKI as a partner, that brings in veterinary and agricultural institutions to prevent, detect and control AMR and zoonotic diseases in four African countries.
projects.note: FLI is Germany's federal animal health institute, not an NPHI; RKI takes part as a partner.

projects.institutes: Eastern Mediterranean Public Health Network (EMPHNET, Amman; regional scope)
projects.title: RKI–EMPHNET Memorandum of Understanding
projects.summary: A strategic MoU signed in Berlin in October 2024 covering training, research, outbreak response, laboratory management, IPC, AMR, emergency preparedness and support for establishing NPHIs in the Eastern Mediterranean.
projects.note: Jordan is EMPHNET's host country; the work is regional.

projects.actor: European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC)
projects.institutes: Country signatories not named on the page
projects.title: ECDC MoUs with EU Enlargement countries
projects.summary: MoUs signed in Stockholm on 28 April 2025 that formalise 14 years of cooperation. They cover information exchange on cross-border threats, observer participation in ECDC networks, and are a prerequisite for data-sharing agreements.
projects.note: ECDC is an EU agency, not an NPHI.

projects.institutes: Gulf Center for Disease Prevention and Control (Gulf CDC, Riyadh; GCC regional body)
projects.title: Gulf CDC delegation technical exchange at China CDC
projects.summary: A Gulf CDC delegation led by CEO Pasi Penttinen visited China CDC in September 2025 for technical exchanges on disease-control systems, surveillance, emergency response, immunisation and training.
projects.note: No agreement was signed. Gulf CDC also visited ECDC in June 2025, where both sides said they intend to formalise their partnership (https://www.ecdc.europa.eu/en/news-events/gulf-health-council-and-gulf-cdc-visit-ecdc). Saudi Arabia is listed as Gulf CDC's host country.

projects.institutes: Network of University Medicine (NUM, Charité-coordinated)
projects.title: JIHS–NUM MoU on infection research and crisis preparedness
projects.summary: An MoU signed in Berlin on 15 April 2026 at the first JIHS–NUM symposium, covering joint multicentre studies, exchange of data and methods, staff exchange and crisis preparedness. Topics include viral haemorrhagic fevers and AMR.
projects.note: The MoU is initially valid for three years. JIHS also signed a high-consequence infectious disease preparedness MoU with NYC Health + Hospitals/Bellevue (USA) in June 2025.

projects.institutes: Sierra Leone-China Friendship Biological Safety Laboratory (Freetown); Ministry of Health and Sanitation
projects.title: Sierra Leone–China Friendship BSL-3 laboratory (Ebola response)
projects.summary: During the West African Ebola epidemic, China built a fixed BSL-3 laboratory in Freetown, and China CDC staffed it with rotating teams. The lab began Ebola testing in March 2015 under good-laboratory-practice and biosafety procedures.
projects.note: Described in a Short Report, Infect Dis Poverty 2016;5:62. The project began 20 Nov 2014; the first China CDC team arrived 8 Feb 2015; Ebola testing began 11 Mar 2015 (913 specimens to 20 Apr 2015). The 2015 end year covers only the Ebola mission phase.

projects.institutes: Ministry of Health and Sanitation Sierra Leone; Sierra Leone-China Friendship Biological Safety Laboratory; Sierra Leone-China Friendship Hospital; Public Health England (UK partner)
projects.title: China–UK Global Health project on public health capacity in Sierra Leone
projects.summary: Under the China-UK Global Health Support Programme, China CDC worked with Sierra Leone's Ministry of Health and with Public Health England. Together they set up bacteriology and parasitology labs, wrote SOPs (cholera, typhoid, malaria microscopy), trained local technicians and supported outbreak and COVID-19 testing.
projects.note: Described in Xue et al., China CDC Weekly 2025;7(1):27-30 (DOI 10.46234/ccdcw2025.006). The article names PHE as the UK partner. No end date is given.

projects.institutes: Instituto Nacional de Saúde (Mozambique); INSP Angola; INASA (Guinea-Bissau); IHMT Lisbon; ISPUP Porto; INSP Cabo Verde (created 2014); São Tomé and Príncipe participants
projects.title: Structuring cooperation and the RINSP-CPLP network of national public health institutes
projects.summary: Fiocruz started exploratory missions in 2006 (with IANPHI and US CDC support) that led to the network of national public health institutes of Portuguese-speaking countries (RINSP-CPLP), founded in Bissau in 2011. Through it Fiocruz supported institute creation, strategic planning and master's programmes in Mozambique, Angola, Guinea-Bissau and Cabo Verde.
projects.type: Structuring cooperation / NPHI network (described in article)
projects.note: Described in Rosenberg et al., An Inst Hig Med Trop 2016;15(Supl.1):S19-S26. Meetings were held 2011, 2013, 2014 (Ebola seminar in Maputo) and 2016. Cabo Verde and São Tomé and Príncipe are not in the atlas and appear only here.

projects.institutes: Instituto Nacional de Saúde (INS-MZ); Ministry of Health of Mozambique; Fiocruz Africa office (Maputo, since 2008)
projects.title: Brazil–Mozambique health cooperation: strengthening Mozambique's INS
projects.summary: Within Brazil–Mozambique technical cooperation, Fiocruz supported the development of Mozambique's National Health Institute, along with postgraduate training, a human milk bank and an antiretroviral factory. The INS development is described as perhaps the biggest success of Brazilian health cooperation.
projects.note: Analysed in Pereira, Ciênc Saúde Coletiva 2017;22(7):2267-76. Much of the work ran under PAHO TC 41 (Dec 2005 to Dec 2015). This is a Brazil-led bilateral item, separate from the excluded 'Mozambique INS peer learning'.

projects.institutes: Institutes leading work packages in France, Bulgaria and Greece; Spanish national public health institute (training); Padua Teaching Hospital; 26 member countries in total across southern Europe, the Balkans, North Africa and the Middle East (not all named in the article)
projects.title: EpiSouth Mediterranean/Balkan communicable disease network
projects.summary: An ISS-coordinated network linking public health institutes and ministries around the Mediterranean and in the Balkans. Its work covered cross-border epidemic intelligence, vaccine-preventable diseases and migrants, emerging zoonoses, and training.
projects.note: Described in Dente et al., Euro Surveill 2009;14(5):19113. The end year 2014 (EpiSouth 2006-2010, then EpiSouth Plus 2010-2014) comes from an EU capacity4dev document, not from the article. Only the EU partner countries are named in the article.

projects.institutes: Institut National de Santé Publique (INSP), DRC; also IANPHI, Africa CDC, WHO, Jhpiego
projects.title: Support to establish DRC's National Public Health Institute
projects.summary: At the DRC government's request, US CDC supported the set-up of the national public health institute from 2018. This included a technical working group that drafted the roadmap, plans and organogram, leading to the institute's creation by decree in April 2022 and its start of operations in September 2022.
projects.note: Described in Angendu et al., PAMJ Clinical Medicine 2024;49:80 (lessons learned 2018-2024). Sciensano and RKI are not mentioned.

projects.institutes: Deployments bilaterally and through WHO GOARN; academic partners LSHTM, Oxford, King's College London
projects.title: UK Public Health Rapid Support Team (UK-PHRST)
projects.summary: A PHE–academic team that deploys within 48 hours to outbreaks in low- and middle-income countries and also does research and capacity building. Deployments included cholera in Ethiopia, the 2017 Freetown mudslides, plague in Madagascar, and early COVID-19 deployments to Asia and Africa.
projects.type: Outbreak response & research partnership (case study article)
projects.note: Described in Raftery, Hossain & Palmer, BMC Public Health 2021;21:1378. Launched 2016 (funded April 2016, official launch November 2016). The article does not give a current status.

projects.institutes: National Institute for Communicable Diseases (NICD), South Africa
projects.title: North/South NPHI collaboration England–South Africa
projects.summary: A peer partnership between the English and South African national public health institutes that shared expertise, supported IHR implementation and built health-protection capacity. It was presented as a model for global health protection that benefits both sides.
projects.note: Ihekweazu, Ncube, Schoub, Blumberg et al., J Public Health Policy 2015;36(2):181-93 (PMID 25568964). Start and end years are not stated on the page opened, which is a bibliographic record, not the journal page.

projects.institutes: Public Health Center of the Ministry of Health of Ukraine; Ministry of Health of Ukraine; regional hospitals in Ternopil, Khmelnytskyi and Vinnytsia; WHO Europe; ICAP; ESCMID
projects.title: Wartime antimicrobial resistance response in Ukraine
projects.summary: From mid-2022, US CDC, Ukraine's Public Health Center and partners assessed infection control and laboratory capacity in three regions and ran point-prevalence surveys. The surveys found that 60% of healthcare-associated infections involved carbapenem-resistant organisms; the partners then supported training, lab upgrades and guidance.
projects.type: Joint response/research (MMWR Notes from the Field)
projects.note: Kuzin et al., MMWR 2023;72(49).

projects.institutes: UK Health Security Agency; IANPHI
projects.title: IANPHI climate roadmap: NPHIs as climate actors
projects.summary: Santé publique France and UKHSA, with IANPHI, wrote and promoted a roadmap (launched at COP26) on how national public health institutes should take part in climate adaptation and mitigation.
projects.note: Pascal, Phalkey, Rigal et al., Lancet Public Health 2022;7(3):e209. The roadmap was launched in November 2021 (SpF page). 'Ongoing' rests on IANPHI 2025 meeting material.

projects.institutes: Instituto Nacional de Laboratorios de Salud (INLASA), Bolivia
projects.title: Peru INS – Bolivia INLASA peer-to-peer partnership
projects.summary: INLASA visited INS Peru in April 2014 to start a cooperation on lab diagnosis, surveillance and research. INS was also to give technical help with INLASA's system assessment and strategic plan. Both sides planned a long-term twinning, with expert exchanges that IANPHI might fund.
projects.note: Twinning was only planned; the source does not say whether it went ahead.

projects.institutes: Public Health Institute of Malawi (PHIM); Malawi Ministry of Health
projects.title: NIPH–IANPHI workshop for the new Public Health Institute of Malawi
projects.summary: In February 2014, NIPH and IANPHI held a workshop to plan the structure of the newly created PHIM: a reference library, an epidemiology unit and a research unit. NIPH and IANPHI were to keep giving technical help.

projects.institutes: Institut National d'Hygiène (INH) Togo; Institut de Veille Sanitaire (InVS) France
projects.title: Strengthening the information system of Togo's INH
projects.summary: IPM and InVS gave pro-bono help, with IANPHI funding, to assess INH Togo's information system and recommend improvements. IPM also offered on-site help, study visits to Morocco and an internship. A related item: IPM secured lab equipment for INH with IANPHI support.
projects.note: The status is inferred: these were 2013 activities.

projects.institutes: INH Togo; University of Lomé; National Blood Transfusion Center Lomé
projects.title: InVS–Togo mentorship, scientific-writing training and research protocols
projects.summary: InVS mentored the INH Togo director under the IANPHI/Heymann mentorship programme. In April 2013 it trained 19 West African scientists in scientific writing, using cases from Togo and Côte d'Ivoire, and supported five Togolese research protocols.
projects.note: The source says the mentorship started about two years before 2013, so 2011 is approximate. The protocols were planned over 12–18 months.

projects.title: Zambia and Malawi peer visit to Mozambique
projects.summary: In 2015, delegations from Zambia and Malawi visited Mozambique to learn how an NPHI is set up and how it works with the Ministry of Health.
projects.note: The case study does not name the institutes. The host is inferred as INS Mozambique.

projects.institutes: National Institute of Health (NIH) Islamabad; Public Health England; US CDC
projects.title: Planning week at RIVM to turn NIH Islamabad into Pakistan's NPHI
projects.summary: In 2017, a Pakistani NIH and ministry delegation spent a week at RIVM with IANPHI, PHE and US CDC. Together they drafted a vision, a mission and an action plan for turning NIH into a comprehensive NPHI.

projects.institutes: Institut National de Santé Publique (INSP) Burkina Faso; Sciensano
projects.title: Burkina Faso INSP peer visit to Santé publique France and Sciensano
projects.summary: In July 2019, six leaders of Burkina Faso's new merged NPHI visited Santé publique France and Sciensano. They looked at governance, internal control, reference labs, the emergency operations centre, communications and research.

projects.institutes: WIV-ISP (Belgium, evaluated); RKI; Fiocruz; InVS; Emory GHI / IANPHI US office; US CDC
projects.title: IANPHI peer-to-peer evaluation of Belgium's WIV-ISP
projects.summary: In April 2015, experts from RKI, Fiocruz, InVS and IANPHI carried out an external peer evaluation of Belgium's Scientific Institute of Public Health. A US CDC expert was to review its bioinformatics later that year.

projects.institutes: National Public Health Organization (EODY), Greece; US CDC
projects.title: Staged Development Tool and strategic planning with Greece's EODY
projects.summary: In 2022, IANPHI and US CDC supported EODY's strategic planning and ran the NPHI Staged Development Tool to find areas where the institute could work better.

projects.institutes: Public Health Institute of Malawi (PHIM); GIZ Malawi; Africa CDC; IANPHI
projects.title: Combined Africa CDC Maturity Scorecard and NPHI Staged Development Tool assessment of PHIM
projects.summary: In November 2025, PHIM completed an assessment combining the Africa CDC maturity scorecard with the IANPHI/CDC Staged Development Tool, covering research, labs and surveillance. It was run by NIPH and GIZ with EU and Norwegian funding, with Africa CDC and IANPHI as technical collaborators.
projects.note: The 2025 progress report describes the same event as an IANPHI–Africa CDC mission, 2–7 Nov 2025.

projects.institutes: Institut National de Santé Publique (INSP) Guinea; Guinean Ministry of Health; US CDC; WHO
projects.title: IANPHI-supported infection-control training in Guinea during Ebola
projects.summary: In 2014, during the West African Ebola outbreak, IANPHI worked with Guinea's INSP, CDC and WHO. It funded protective equipment, trained infection-control officers and placed them in health facilities.
projects.note: The end year is not stated.

projects.institutes: INASA Guinea-Bissau; Fiocruz; Instituto de Higiene e Medicina Tropical (IHMT); Nigerian Institute of Medical Research (NIMR)
projects.title: Gates-funded NPHI development grant for Guinea-Bissau's INASA
projects.summary: IANPHI gave INASA a three-year NPHI development grant and was the first donor for its headquarters, opened in February 2011. Fiocruz and IHMT advised on rebuilding the lab and on disease monitoring, and NIMR's director mentored INASA's director.
projects.note: The exact grant years are not stated (the 2010–2012 report covers it). Status is inferred.

projects.institutes: Uganda Virus Research Institute (UVRI)
projects.title: NIMR technical assistance to UVRI on financial management
projects.summary: Within IANPHI's comprehensive projects, NIMR helped UVRI set up a financial management system and a research support office. About US$16M was leveraged afterwards.
projects.note: Years are not stated (2010–2012 report). Status is inferred.

projects.actor: Finnish Institute for Health and Welfare (THL)
projects.institutes: National Institute for Medical Research (NIMR) Tanzania
projects.title: THL–NIMR Tanzania partnership on NCD surveillance
projects.summary: Under an IANPHI comprehensive project running since 2007, Finland's THL partnered with Tanzania's NIMR to strengthen surveillance and prevention of non-communicable diseases. This included an IANPHI-supported NCD workshop in 2011.
projects.note: The report says IANPHI worked with NIMR since 2007. The THL start year is not stated.

projects.institutes: China CDC (evaluated); experts from Morocco, Norway, China and the US (led by Jeffrey Koplan)
projects.title: IANPHI evaluation team review of China CDC
projects.summary: In 2011, an IANPHI evaluation team led by Jeffrey Koplan, with experts from Morocco, Norway, China and the US, reviewed China CDC.
projects.note: The report does not name the Moroccan and Norwegian institutes.

projects.title: Thailand NIH regional laboratory collaboration
projects.summary: In an IANPHI-funded project, Thailand's NIH worked with labs in Cambodia, Laos, Myanmar and Bhutan on techniques, biosafety and external quality assurance. In 2012 it coordinated with Cambodia and Vietnam on hand, foot and mouth disease outbreaks.
projects.note: Partner institutes are not named. Laos also took part in cholera research.

projects.institutes: Public Health Center of Ukraine; WHO Regional Office for Europe; merged NPHIs of Belgium, France, Norway, Sweden, UK
projects.title: Joint WHO Europe–IANPHI seminars on building NPHIs through mergers
projects.summary: WHO Europe and IANPHI held three seminars, in Kyiv (2017), Warsaw (2018) and Moldova (April 2019). Merged NPHIs from Belgium, France, Norway, Sweden and the UK shared their experience with countries setting up NPHIs: Ukraine, Moldova, Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan, with Albania joining in 2019.
projects.note: France also shared its experience. Poland is listed because it hosted the 2018 seminar.

projects.institutes: Polish national public health institute (host)
projects.title: IANPHI Europe mission to the Poland–Ukraine border
projects.summary: In May 2022, Poland's NPHI invited an IANPHI Europe delegation to visit refugee reception sites on the Ukrainian border. The mission produced a report with recommendations.
projects.note: The report does not name the Polish institute.

projects.actor: Uganda National Institute of Public Health (UNIPH)
projects.title: UNIPH peer exchange with Kenya and Rwanda on border health risk mapping
projects.summary: In 2022, with IANPHI/US CDC support for border health, UNIPH worked with Kenya and Rwanda on peer-to-peer training and exchange on health risk mapping.
projects.note: Partner institutes are not named. This is part of CDC-funded IANPHI country work.

projects.actor: Institut National de Santé Publique (INSP) Côte d'Ivoire
projects.institutes: NPHIs of Burkina Faso, DRC and Mali; WAHO; US CDC; IANPHI; TEPHINET
projects.title: Côte d'Ivoire public health bulletin and Francophone bulletin exchange
projects.summary: INSP Côte d'Ivoire launched its public health bulletin (BSP-CI) in April 2023 with CDC/IANPHI support. In August 2024 it hosted a Francophone peer exchange workshop in Abidjan on bulletins with Burkina Faso, DRC and Mali.
projects.note: A community of practice was planned; its status is unclear.

projects.institutes: National Institute of Public Health (NIPH) Cambodia; Institut Pasteur du Cambodge
projects.title: IANPHI support to Cambodia's NIPH
projects.summary: IANPHI has worked with Cambodia's NIPH since 2016, with Gates Foundation and CDC funding, on a research strategy and blended learning at its School of Public Health. It also gave early COVID-19 support: lab training, protective equipment and test reagents.
projects.note: May partly fall under the CDC–IANPHI cooperative agreement.

projects.institutes: Instituto Nacional de Saúde (INS) Mozambique; Kenyan One Health experts
projects.title: One Health and vector-borne/zoonotic surveillance support to INS Mozambique
projects.summary: In 2020, IANPHI's Mozambique project built INS capacity in vector-borne and zoonotic surveillance and One Health. The Oswaldo Cruz Institute (Brazil) and Kenyan One Health experts were collaborators.
projects.note: The Kenyan institute is not named.

projects.institutes: INS Mozambique; NIH Pakistan; others not named
projects.title: Gates-funded Integrated Disease Surveillance project
projects.summary: In 2022, IANPHI ran a Gates-funded study of integrated disease surveillance. It made country deep dives in Mozambique, Pakistan, Malawi, Uganda, England, Sweden and Canada, and held a webinar with NIH Pakistan and INS Mozambique.

projects.title: Multicentric project on territorial health inequalities
projects.summary: Fiocruz leads a US CDC-funded project on territorial health inequalities in five Latin American countries. IANPHI reports it under its Social and Public Health Inequalities Committee.
projects.note: Start year and partner institutes are not stated. 'Ongoing' is an assumption from the 2025 report.

projects.institutes: RIVM; Public Health Scotland
projects.title: IANPHI Planetary Health subgroup workshop at EPH Conference 2025
projects.summary: Staff from RKI, RIVM and Public Health Scotland co-hosted a workshop of the IANPHI Planetary Health subgroup at the 2025 European Public Health Conference in Helsinki.
projects.note: This is a climate-committee activity, separate from the excluded SpF/UKHSA roadmap and WMO MoU.

projects.institutes: European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC)
projects.title: IANPHI–ECDC Memorandum of Understanding
projects.summary: In 2025, IANPHI and ECDC signed an MoU in Maputo. It covers preparedness and response, surveillance, training, climate impacts on communicable diseases, and communication.
projects.note: ECDC is an EU agency, not an NPHI; Sweden is listed as its seat. The secretariat was moving to RKI during 2025.

projects.institutes: US CDC Vietnam office
projects.title: IANPHI–CDC support for creating a Vietnam NPHI
projects.summary: In 2022, IANPHI and US CDC consulted CDC-Vietnam staff, and a joint team travelled to Vietnam to support efforts to create a national public health institute.
projects.note: No Vietnamese institute is named.

projects.institutes: INASA (Guinea-Bissau, then in creation); Instituto Nacional de Saúde (INS) Mozambique
projects.title: Fiocruz–IANPHI peer-assistance planning with Guinea-Bissau and Mozambique
projects.summary: In 2006, Fiocruz and IANPHI held a meeting of NPHIs from Portuguese-speaking countries. In 2007 this led to two Fiocruz peer-assistance planning sessions: a 5-year plan to create an NPHI in Guinea-Bissau, and a plan to strengthen Mozambique's existing institute.
projects.note: This is the start of the INASA project in agent_ianphi.json. It is bilateral IANPHI work, separate from the excluded RINSP-CPLP network. The IANPHI 10-year report lists Mozambique–Brazil as a twinning pair.

projects.institutes: Uganda Virus Research Institute (UVRI); US CDC
projects.title: HPA and US CDC partnership on UVRI's 5-year strategic plan
projects.summary: In 2007, under IANPHI, the UK Health Protection Agency and US CDC worked with UVRI on its 5-year strategic plan and the systems work linked to it.
projects.note: The end year is not stated, and 'completed' is inferred. This is distinct from the excluded HPA–NICD item.

projects.institutes: Instituto Nacional de Salud (INS) Colombia; International Development Research Centre (IDRC, Canada)
projects.title: PHAC/IDRC–INS Colombia chronic disease surveillance project in Pasto
projects.summary: An IANPHI project in which Colombia's INS partnered with PHAC and Canada's IDRC on chronic disease surveillance and research in Pasto.
projects.note: Only the 2007 report mentions it; the end year is not stated.

projects.title: IANPHI Ebola preparedness support to West and Central African countries
projects.summary: In 2014–2015, IANPHI and its members gave funds and technical help to Guinea, Cameroon, Côte d'Ivoire and Guinea-Bissau. The help covered case-management training, prevention messages, protective equipment, specimen handling, screening at 40 border points and rapid response teams. The project list also includes Ebola preparedness in Togo.
projects.note: Guinea is left out because it is a separate entry (ianphi-guinea-ebola-ipc-2014). Partner institutes are not named.

projects.institutes: Instituto Nacional de Saúde (INS) Mozambique; National Institute for Medical Research (NIMR) Tanzania
projects.title: IANPHI Leadership Academy for African NPHI leaders
projects.summary: IANPHI launched a Leadership Academy in 2014 with backing from Sweden's NPHI and the Gates Foundation. INS Mozambique and NIMR Tanzania gave local support, and a Kenyan participant went on to become a Heymann Fellow.
projects.note: Kenya is listed only because of the trainee. The academy's duration is not stated.

projects.title: Laying the foundation for a Somali NPHI
projects.summary: IANPHI lists a project to lay the groundwork for a national public health institute in Somalia through advocacy and peer-to-peer assistance.
projects.note: No dates and no partner institutes are given; the report covers roughly 2006–2016.

projects.institutes: National Public Health Institute of Liberia (NPHIL); US CDC; WHO
projects.title: Support for creating the National Public Health Institute of Liberia
projects.summary: After Ebola, IANPHI ran a project to create a Liberian NPHI, with WHO and US CDC. The NPHI Act was signed in January 2017, and IANPHI published a case study on its legal framework.
projects.note: The start year is not given; the context is the 2014–15 Ebola outbreak. The 10-year report also lists the Liberia NPHI project. No peer-NPHI partner is named, and the US is listed for US CDC.

projects.institutes: Sierra Leone Ministry of Health and Sanitation
projects.title: Strategic planning for a Sierra Leone NPHI
projects.summary: IANPHI supported strategic planning to set up a national public health agency in Sierra Leone. Sierra Leone also asked for an NPHI-to-NPHI evaluation through the IANPHI service launched in 2011.
projects.note: Undated. The evaluation request comes from the 2010–2012 progress report, and no completed evaluation was found.

projects.institutes: UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA); WHO Regional Office for Europe
projects.title: WHO Europe reference group supporting public health in Azerbaijan
projects.summary: In 2023, IANPHI and UKHSA colleagues joined a WHO Europe reference group supporting the development of Azerbaijan's public health institutions.

projects.institutes: World Health Organization (WHO)
projects.title: IANPHI–WHO agreement on NPHI creation and development
projects.summary: In 2022, IANPHI and WHO signed what IANPHI calls a historic agreement to support creating and developing NPHIs, with a two-year joint action plan to follow.
projects.note: WHO is not an NPHI; Switzerland is listed as WHO's seat. In 2023 WHO and IANPHI also co-organised an EPHF consultation workshop.

projects.title: SSI Strategic Sector Cooperation – Tanzania
projects.summary: Danish government-to-government health cooperation led by SSI. It covers disease surveillance, diagnostic quality, AMR monitoring and capacity building.
projects.note: SSI's page does not name a partner institute. Status is inferred because the page presents it as current work. NIMR Tanzania reported a Danish SSC scoping visit on 23 Apr 2025 covering One Health, AMR and climate (nimr.or.tz).

projects.title: SSI Strategic Sector Cooperation – Ukraine
projects.summary: Danish SSC support for Ukraine's public health resilience, infectious disease preparedness and data-driven surveillance during reconstruction.
projects.note: Years and partner institute are not stated. Status is inferred.

projects.title: SSI Strategic Sector Cooperation – India
projects.summary: SSI cooperation with India on infectious disease preparedness, AMR surveillance and One Health laboratory systems.
projects.note: Years and partner institute are not stated. Status is inferred.

projects.institutes: Centre for Biosecurity and Biopreparedness (SSI); Kenyan agencies and life-science universities
projects.title: Kenya biosecurity and biopreparedness partnership
projects.summary: A six-year partnership programme that helped Kenya draft and implement biosecurity legislation. It also built biopreparedness capacity in agencies and raised awareness at universities.
projects.note: The fact sheet says six years but gives no start or end year.

projects.institutes: Federal Ministry of Health and Human Services Somalia; National Institute of Health Somalia; WHO Somalia; NIRAS Sweden AB
projects.title: Establishment of Somalia National Institute of Health
projects.summary: Sida-funded support led by FHM to set up an independent Somali NIH, working with WHO under a non-financial MoU signed in December 2020. Areas covered include workforce, surveillance, emergency response and health information.
projects.note: Openaid lists it as closed, running 1 Jun 2019 to 30 Apr 2026, with SEK 24.2m paid. The WHO MoU is at emro.who.int.

projects.institutes: Public Health Center of Ukraine; WHO Country Office Ukraine; regional CDCs; Kharkiv National Medical University; Zdorovi primary care network
projects.title: AMR Contain – support to Ukraine
projects.summary: Supports Ukraine's national action plan on AMR and healthcare-associated infections. Work covers AMR and antibiotic-use data, stewardship, IPC guidelines, laboratory capacity and One Health coordination.
projects.note: Nordic coordination with SSI and NIPH/FHI.

projects.institutes: Africa CDC; IANPHI; WHO (multilateral collaborators)
projects.title: Building Stronger Public Health Institutions and Systems (BIS), Phase 2
projects.summary: Norad-funded programme to strengthen public health institutes in four core partner countries, with selected BIS-1 activities continuing in Uganda and Ghana. Themes are climate and health, digital health, infectious diseases, NCDs and evidence-informed decision-making.
projects.note: Umbrella entry. Remove it if it overlaps the excluded 'NIPH partner countries' item.

projects.institutes: Public Health Institute of Malawi (PHIM)
projects.title: BIS collaboration in Malawi
projects.summary: Institutional support to PHIM as it may become an autonomous body. Includes a new MMed in public health, surveillance gap analysis (IDSR) and biosecurity courses tied to Malawi's JEE.
projects.note: NIPH has collaborated with PHIM since 2008.

projects.institutes: Public Health Institute of Malawi; Norwegian Church Aid; IANPHI; I-TECH; WHO
projects.title: Global Health Preparedness Project in Malawi
projects.summary: Seconded expertise and funding to strengthen IDSR and IHR core capacities. Activities included the 2019 JEE, national health security action planning, FETP, an Ebola simulation and cholera, anthrax and COVID-19 responses.
projects.note: The page was last updated in 2022.

projects.institutes: Kathmandu University School of Medical Sciences; CAIPHEN consortium; Nepal Health Research Council; Planetary Health Research Centre; Tribhuvan University; National Public Health Laboratory; Ministry of Health and Population
projects.title: BIS collaboration in Nepal
projects.summary: Supports evidence-informed policy, implementation research fellowships, public health education and NGS/bioinformatics training. Also includes planetary health courses and a climate–dengue case study.
projects.note: Phase 1 ran 2023–25 and Phase 2 runs 2025–29.

projects.institutes: Nepal Health Research Council
projects.title: Dengue and climate change case study, Nepal
projects.summary: NIPH supported NHRC in producing an in-depth case study of how climate change shapes dengue in Nepal.
projects.note: Listed as a previous project. Years are not given.

projects.institutes: Ethiopian Public Health Institute
projects.title: BIS Ethiopia: Climate, Nutrition and Health Hub / Knowledge Hub and EthAir
projects.summary: NIPH supports a cross-divisional Climate, Nutrition and Health Hub at EPHI, local evidence on climate-sensitive risks and air-pollution studies (EthAir household survey and low-cost sensor monitoring). It also funds AMR and biosafety capacity work.
projects.note: Distinct from the excluded EPHI peer exchange, but drop it if that exclusion covers all EPHI work. EthAir belonged to BIS phase 1 (2022–25).

projects.institutes: Palestinian National Institute of Public Health; Palestinian Ministry of Health; WHO country office; University of Oslo
projects.title: BIS collaboration in Palestine
projects.summary: More than a decade of support to build PNIPH into a sustainable national institute. Work covers surveillance, registries, the MCH eRegistry and IHR core capacities.
projects.note: PNIPH was set up as a WHO project in 2012. Palestine is a BIS-2 partner.

projects.institutes: Public Health Center of Ukraine; Sunnaas hospital (NO)
projects.title: Public health collaboration between Ukraine and Norway
projects.summary: Strategic and technical twinning to build the capacity of the Public Health Center of Ukraine in IPC, crisis preparedness and health data. Later added mental health and rehabilitation training in war-affected areas.

projects.institutes: University College London; RAND Corporation; University of the West Indies; University of Oslo
projects.title: Belmont Forum: Community collective action on climate change and the environment–health nexus
projects.summary: Comparative study of how volunteer community groups in Alaska and Trinidad and Tobago organise to respond to climate-related health impacts, aimed at informing health-system resilience planning.
projects.note: NIPH lists itself as a partner on fhi.no/en/globalhealth/climate-and-health/our-projects/. The Belmont page names University of Oslo staff. The 36-month duration from the 2020 award gives an estimated end year. Trinidad and Tobago may not be in the 110m atlas.

projects.institutes: Institut Pasteur de Dakar
projects.title: UKHSA–Institut Pasteur de Dakar strategic partnership (MoU)
projects.summary: A 2024 MoU on co-developing vaccines and diagnostics for emerging threats, early detection and surveillance in Senegal and West Africa, and epidemic laboratory capacity. Rapid tests for measles and onchocerciasis are among the outputs.
projects.note: IPD's mission to the UK took place 26–30 Jan 2025.

projects.institutes: Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency
projects.title: UKHSA–KDCA memorandum of understanding on health security
projects.summary: MoU covering preparedness and response, VHF outbreak monitoring, laboratory capacity, AMR and IPC, immunisation policy, pathogen data sharing and staff exchanges.
projects.note: Signed 9 May 2022.

projects.actor: Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency
projects.institutes: Lao Ministry of Health (Dept. of Communicable Disease Control; National Centre for Laboratory and Epidemiology); Hanyang University College of Medicine
projects.title: SHEPERD – Strengthening Health Emergencies Preparedness and Enhancing Response to Disease Outbreaks
projects.summary: KDCA-funded bilateral ODA that builds Lao laboratory systems and hospital-based surveillance for acute febrile illness and gastroenteritis. In 2026 it held the first Korea–Laos MERS tabletop exercise.
projects.note: KDCA's own page gives 2022–2026.

projects.actor: Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency
projects.title: KDCA–Mongolia laboratory capacity cooperation
projects.summary: Building Mongolia's national laboratory capacity, joint training on emerging infectious diseases and provision of quarantine supplies.

projects.actor: Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency
projects.institutes: Africa CDC; International Vaccine Institute
projects.title: KDCA support to Africa CDC
projects.summary: Supports Africa CDC's crisis response, infectious disease diagnosis and capacity building in laboratory specimen transport and management. Africa CDC, IVI and KDCA also announced a vaccine-access and health-security partnership at the June 2024 Korea–Africa Summit.
projects.note: Ethiopia is a placeholder for Africa CDC's Addis Ababa HQ. The real scope is continental. Summit details: ivi.int.

projects.actor: Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency
projects.institutes: ASEAN Secretariat
projects.title: KDCA support to ASEAN infectious disease early warning and risk assessment
projects.summary: Funds and supports the operation of an ASEAN regional system for infectious disease early warning and risk assessment.
projects.note: The partner list is the ASEAN members. Singapore is not in the atlas.

projects.actor: Finnish Institute for Health and Welfare (THL)
projects.institutes: Public Health Center of Ukraine; Ministry of Health of Ukraine; GFA Consulting Group (co-implementer)
projects.title: Support to Ukraine for Developing a Modern Public Health System
projects.summary: EU-funded project (€5.8m) co-implemented by THL. It strengthened the Ukrainian Public Health Centre, aligned surveillance and response legislation with the EU, reformed blood safety and trained more than 1,500 professionals.

projects.institutes: National Public Health Institute of Kenya; Kenya Medical Research Institute (KEMRI); TNO; Kenyan Ministry of Health; Dutch Ministry of Health, Welfare and Sport
projects.title: Kenya–Netherlands climate and health partnership
projects.summary: Bilateral health-ministry partnership in which RIVM and Kenya's NPHI work on a climate change and health vulnerability and adaptation assessment. It also covers guidelines for green, climate-resilient healthcare facilities and knowledge exchange.
projects.note: Article of 6 Jun 2024. Joint initiatives were planned for 2024–2025, and the implementation plan was still to be finalised. No follow-up was verified.

projects.actor: Institut National de Santé Publique (INSP) Côte d'Ivoire
projects.institutes: Institut de recherche pour le développement (IRD); Institut Pierre Richet (Bouaké)
projects.title: INSP–IRD framework agreement on scientific and technical cooperation
projects.summary: Framework agreement to strengthen research capacity at the Institut Pierre Richet in Bouaké against vector-borne diseases. INSP asked for the scope to be extended to nutrition, maternal and child health and metabolic disease.
projects.note: Signed around 1 Apr 2014, following a headquarters agreement of 7 Feb 2013. Duration is not stated.

projects.institutes: WHO Regional Office for Europe (Copenhagen)
projects.title: Scale-Up Integrate – HIV, viral hepatitis and STI monitoring and elimination in the WHO European Region
projects.summary: Follow-up to Scale-up HIVHEP that supports WHO EURO member states in integrated surveillance, control and elimination of HIV, hepatitis B/C and sexually transmitted infections.
projects.note: Region-wide (WHO EURO); Denmark = seat of WHO EURO, no individual countries named

projects.actor: Bernhard Nocht Institute for Tropical Medicine (BNITM)
projects.institutes: Irrua Specialist Teaching Hospital (Nigeria); Abubakar Tafawa Balewa University Teaching Hospital (Nigeria); Federal Medical Centre Owo (Nigeria); Laboratoire des Fièvres Hémorragiques Virales de Cotonou (Benin); CIPEC IST/VIH/Sida Parakou (Benin); LFHVG Conakry (Guinea); LFHV Guéckédou (Guinea); LFHV Hôpital régional de N'Zérékoré (Guinea); Njala University (Sierra Leone); Robert Koch Institute (Germany)
projects.title: AfroLabNet3 – Laboratory networks and mobile response capacity for pandemic preparedness
projects.summary: Third phase of the BNITM laboratory network strengthening fixed and mobile lab capacity to detect viral haemorrhagic fevers and other emerging pathogens in West Africa, with a One Health angle.
projects.note: RKI is a partner institution

projects.institutes: WHO / GOARN Operational Support Team (Geneva)
projects.title: GOARN_CC_II – WHO Collaborating Centre for GOARN
projects.summary: RKI operates as WHO Collaborating Centre supporting GOARN partners in outbreak preparedness and response through training, workforce development, community engagement and network partnerships.
projects.note: Global scope; Switzerland = WHO/GOARN seat

projects.institutes: Centre Hospitalier et Universitaire de Bouaké (Côte d'Ivoire); Johanniter-Unfall-Hilfe e.V. (Germany); Bernhard-Nocht-Institut für Tropenmedizin (Germany)
projects.title: SMILE – Strengthening mobile laboratory capacities for health emergencies
projects.summary: Builds mobile laboratory capacity for emergency response in Côte d'Ivoire and The Gambia, including staff training, interoperability with Emergency Medical Teams and a West African mobile lab network.

projects.institutes: Ministry of Health Guinea – Direction Régionale de la Santé Faranah; Direction Préfectorale de la Santé Faranah; Faranah Regional Hospital; Institut National de Santé Publique (Conakry)
projects.title: PASQUALE 4-S – Patient safety and care partnership, final sustainability phase
projects.summary: Final phase anchoring infection prevention and control and nosocomial infection surveillance in hospitals of Guinea's Faranah region, incl. local hand-rub production and a study of post-caesarean surgical site infections.

projects.institutes: WHO EMT Secretariat (WHO HQ); WHO Regional Office for Europe; WHO Regional Office for Africa; Lviv Regional Center for Emergency Medical Care and Disaster Medicine (Ukraine); Ministry of Health and Social Services (Namibia); Ministry of Health (Malawi); Institute of Emergency Care of Sarajevo Canton (Bosnia and Herzegovina); Arbeiter-Samariter-Bund; CADUS e.V.; humedica; Johanniter-Unfall-Hilfe (Germany)
projects.title: EMT ReCaP – Emergency Medical Team response capacities and partnerships
projects.summary: Strengthens Emergency Medical Team crisis response in the WHO AFRO and EURO regions through twinning with German EMTs, cross-regional exchange and communities of practice.

projects.institutes: South African Health Products Regulatory Authority; Namibia Medicines Regulatory Council; National Drug Authority (Uganda); Food and Drugs Authority Ghana; Tanzania Medicines and Medical Devices Authority; Zambia Medicines Regulatory Authority; Medicines Control Authority of Zimbabwe; AUDA-NEPAD; Africa Society for Blood Transfusion; WHO AFRO; WHO HQ
projects.title: BloodTrain Chapter III – Availability, quality and safety of blood and blood products in Africa
projects.summary: Third chapter of PEI's support to African regulators to strengthen and harmonise regulation of blood and blood products.

projects.actor: Bernhard Nocht Institute for Tropical Medicine (BNITM)
projects.institutes: Irrua Specialist Teaching Hospital (Nigeria); LFHV Guéckédou (Guinea); Infectious Diseases Unit, University of Parakou / CHU Borgou-Alibori (Benin); LFHV Cotonou (Benin)
projects.title: MEVIN 2.0 – Advanced clinical management of emerging viral infections
projects.summary: Expands intensive-care capacity, equipment, training and staff retention for treating Lassa fever and other viral haemorrhagic fevers in West Africa, plus a global clinical outbreak response team.

projects.institutes: Institute of Tuberculosis and Lung Diseases (Warsaw, Poland); 'Chiril Draganiuc' Institute of Pneumology (Chișinău, Moldova); 'Marius Nasta' Institute of Pneumology (Bucharest, Romania)
projects.title: XBM:TB phase 2 – Cross-border tuberculosis management Germany–Poland–Moldova–Romania
projects.summary: Structured information-exchange protocols to keep TB treatment continuous for patients moving between Germany and partner countries and to monitor outcomes.

projects.institutes: WHO Regional Office for Europe (Denmark); Sciensano (Belgium)
projects.title: PACT-PHM – Partnerships for population health metrics capacities and tools
projects.summary: Builds national capacity to produce burden-of-disease and other population health metrics and embed them in health information systems for policy use.
projects.note: Also lists 'Sub-Saharan Africa' and 'WHO EURO' as regions
